subject: Provider discovery requires source-authorization controls, assertion-specific freshness, and deep-link vs transactional separation
summary: CHCPBC and CCHPBC registries are authoritative for licensure but explicitly restrict commercial/marketing/fundraising use, so automated commercial ingestion requires terms/legal resolution rather than scraper-first implementation.
CCHPBC warns registration numbers can be abused for fraudulent billing; provider identifiers should be minimized, masked/encrypted, and access-scoped.

Jane Practitioner Search is an opt-in BC beta with availability that may take up to three hours to reflect changes; Jane currently has no open API and its published integration posture does not support AI scheduling or direct calendar posting.
TELUS eClaims has an API for authenticated provider/PMS claims workflows, but this is not evidence of a public provider-discovery API and should be treated as an R2/R10 integration concern.

Canada Life explicitly marks its provider list non-real-time and non-guaranteeing; Sun Life Provider Search mixes claims-derived, provider-entered, and booking/availability fields, requiring field-level provenance.
R3 proposes assertion-specific TTLs, SOURCE_NOT_AUTHORIZED as a first-class freshness/policy state, immutable provider IDs with versioned aliases, and explicit contradiction rules.

cross_lane_handoffs.R2: Treat TELUS eClaims API as authenticated claims/PMS infrastructure, not open discovery; preserve direct-billing vs member-coverage separation.
cross_lane_handoffs.R4: Treat Jane under current policy as discovery/deep-link rather than autonomous scheduling; distinguish DEEP_LINK_HANDOFF from TRANSACTIONAL_API.
cross_lane_handoffs.R5_R9: Review non-commercial registry terms and provider identifier fraud sensitivity; terms authorization should be enforced before acquisition.
cross_lane_handoffs.R10: Add source authorization mode, terms posture, automation level, and TTL policy to adapter contracts.

escalations: Legal/terms review before automated commercial ingestion of CHCPBC/CCHPBC registry data.
Do not scrape/reverse-engineer Jane, Sun Life, Canada Life, or TELUS in place of supported integration paths.
Do not expose full provider billing identifiers beyond minimum operational scope.
